key_insight: LLMs' political tendencies can be quantitatively measured by comparing their voting predictions to verified parliamentary records, revealing systematic party- or ideology-aligned biases that vary by model and prompt.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a reproducible, evidence-based benchmark for detecting and quantifying political bias in large language models using real-world legislative votes.
method: Assemble verified parliamentary voting records (bills, timestamps, party votes) as ground truth.
Prompt LLMs to predict how representatives would vote on the same items; record predicted votes and confidence.
Compare predictions to actual votes to compute party/ideology alignment metrics and bias statistics over time and issue areas.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical, reproducible audit method to detect, quantify, and monitor political bias in models—informing mitigation, model choice, and policy decisions for safer deployments.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: data collection → prompting → prediction → comparison/metrics
Heatmap showing alignment between model predictions and party votes (rows: parties, columns: models)
Time-series plot of bias score over legislative sessions or model versions
Example bill card: bill summary, actual vote breakdown, model prediction and confidence
paper_title: Uncovering Political Bias in Large Language Models using Parliamentary Voting Records
paper_authors: Jieying Chen, Karen de Jong, Andreas Poole, Jan Burakowski, Elena Elderson Nosti
